novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new mechanism-level hypothesis—“a small set of attention heads is causally responsible for maintaining an agent's outdated (false) belief”—rather than merely a new setting, with the key prediction being a dissociation between belief-world divergence and true world-state tracking. The closest prior work found was “Language Models Represent Beliefs of Self and Others” (ICML 2024), located using searches for “LLM false belief mechanistic interpretability,” “attention heads belief tracking,” “belief representations self and others language models,” and “Sally-Anne circuit,” which decodes and causally manipulates belief representations but does not identify dedicated attention-head circuitry maintaining stale beliefs. The step from that work to this claim is a substantive new core relationship—head-level causal routing and protection of pre-update state—rather than a direct transfer, although it uses standard interpretability methods and therefore supports high within-paradigm novelty rather than a paradigm-level score.
